newsitem.title: UK: Agents and airlines to action UK messaging.
newsitem.headline: Agents and airlines to action UK messaging.

text.p: British freight forwarders and airlines said in a statement that they have decided to move towards developing an electronic messaging system.

The first public meeting of the Forum for the Advancement of Cargo Electronic Trading in the UK (FACET) resulted in the establishment of a working group to accelerate the pace of electronic mesaging between forwarders and airlines in the UK, FACET said in a statement here.

Some 70 representatives of UK forwarding companies and airline cargo departments met at Heathrow to hear of developments to date in to decide how the UK air cargo market community can speed up the process of electronic communication.

The major benefits of EDI are improved cycle time for shipments, reduced errors, saving in processing costs, better productivity and improved customer service, said project director of IATA's Cargo MEDIA Group of airlines John Hartnett in the statement.
Hartnett said air cargo would lose out to the integrators if immediate positive action to develop electronic communication was not taken on an industry-wide basis.
"Traditionally airfreight service no longer meets customer requirements. If you are offering today services taking over 72 hours, you are simply not in the race," he stated.
Putting the forwarder view, Andy Campbell of BIFA called for early standardisation in order to prevent forwarders from making further IT investments which might subsequently prove pointless.

"I urge the airline community to choose their standard as soon as possible: to publish the standard widely and quickly, so that all forwarders can make some real progress towards electronic trading," he stated.

A recent survey of airfreight agents and airlines in the UK showed a significant number of airlines can process electronic messages but that whilst a number of forwarders already can communicate electronically, others have no form plans to do so, said Bob Alldred of FACET UK. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
